bib.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2020), pages 8342-8360

question: Is it still helpful to tailor a broadly pretrained language model (RoBERTa) to the domain or the unlabeled data of a target task by continuing pretraining?
hypothesis: Where the task data is a narrowly defined subset of a broader domain, pretraining on the task dataset itself or data relevant to it may be helpful; the more dissimilar the domain from RoBERTa's, the higher the potential for DAPT.
contributions: a thorough analysis of domain- and task-adaptive pretraining across four domains and eight tasks, spanning low- and high-resource settings
an investigation into the transferability of adapted LMs across domains and tasks
a study highlighting the importance of pretraining on human-curated datasets, and a simple data selection strategy to automatically approach this performance

method.summary: Continue masked-LM pretraining of RoBERTa-base on large unlabeled domain corpora (DAPT, 12.5K steps), on the task's unlabeled training text (TAPT, 100 epochs), or both in sequence, then fine-tune a classifier on each of eight tasks. Also tests curated extra task text (Curated-TAPT) and VAMPIRE-embedding kNN retrieval of domain sentences (kNN-TAPT).
method.task: continued (adaptive) pretraining followed by text classification fine-tuning

datasets.name: BioMed S2ORC
datasets.source: S2ORC (Lo et al., 2020), internal version incl. papers not releasable

datasets.name: News (REALNEWS)
datasets.preprocessing: summaries and full text, spaCy sentence splitting

datasets.name: Reviews (Amazon)
datasets.preprocessing: entire review body, spaCy sentence splitting

datasets.name: RCT
datasets.preprocessing: all sentences of an abstract in one long sequence for simultaneous prediction

datasets.name: HYPERPARTISAN
datasets.source: Kiesel et al., 2019; splits from Beltagy et al. (2020)

datasets.name: RCT-500
datasets.size: 500 labeled examples (of 180K), rest treated as unlabeled

models.name: RoBERTa-base
models.init_from: off-the-shelf RoBERTa (Liu et al., 2019), pretrained on 160GB text

other.note: called 'off-the-shelf ROBERTA-base model' for the baseline; size not otherwise stated

training.objective: masked LM (cross-entropy on randomly masked tokens), masking probability 0.15
training.lr_schedule: linear decay (Table 13 lists scheduler 'None or warmup linear')
training.batch_size: 2048 effective via gradient accumulation (DAPT); 256 for tasks with <5K examples (TAPT). Table 13 prints '256 or 2058' for the large one.
training.steps: 12.5K steps (DAPT, one pass over each domain dataset)
training.hardware: single Google Cloud v3-8 TPU per adaptive pretraining experiment
training.compute: Table 9 (RCT-500): TAPT 0.2K steps, DAPT 12.5K steps; TAPT nearly 60 times faster than DAPT
training.seeds: five random seeds for fine-tuning; degenerate HYPERPARTISAN seeds discarded and resampled

other.classifier_finetune: final-layer [CLS] -> 1 feedforward layer, tanh, dropout 0.1, batch 16, lr 2e-5, 3 or 10 epochs, patience 3, Quadro RTX 8000 GPU, AllenNLP (Table 14)
other.kNN-TAPT: k = 50, 150 and 500 (Table 8) neighbors per task sentence; RAND-TAPT uses 50 random candidates
other.dapt_corpus_note: corpora sized so each domain sees same data in 12.5K steps

inference.samples: five random seeds per fine-tuning run, mean and std reported
inference.retrieval: kNN-TAPT: VAMPIRE embeddings, k nearest domain sentences per task sentence, flat FAISS index with cosine similarity

metrics.name: macro-F1
metrics.definition: test macro-F1 (all tasks except CHEMPROT, RCT)

metrics.name: micro-F1
metrics.definition: test micro-F1 for CHEMPROT and RCT, following Beltagy et al. 2019

metrics.name: masked LM loss
metrics.definition: RoBERTa MLM loss on 50K held-out docs per domain (Table 1)

baselines: state of the art per task (Table 5 caption)
eval.protocol: Mean over five seeds with standard deviation; test results in main text, dev results in Appendix C (Tables 15-19); no significance test beyond std comparison.

availability.weights: pretrained models for multiple domains and tasks said to be publicly available
availability.data: BioMed and CS use an internal S2ORC version that cannot be fully released

results.quote: TAPT is nearly 60 times faster to train than DAPT on a single v3-8 TPU and storage requirements for DAPT on this task are 5.8M times that of TAPT.

limits: Only RoBERTa-base and only text classification tasks; authors say approaches should apply to any pretrained LM but do not test it.
BioMed and CS corpora use an internal S2ORC version not fully releasable.
Domain boundaries are fuzzy (40% unigram overlap REVIEWS-NEWS); cross-domain MLM loss is a noisy predictor of domain similarity.
HYPERPARTISAN has 65 test examples and high seed variance; degenerate seeds were discarded and resampled.
TAPT then DAPT order, and more sophisticated curricula, are not tested.
Compute in Table 9 is for RCT-500 only; the cost of curating data for Curated-TAPT is not counted.
DAPT/TAPT results do not beat SOTA on several tasks (Table 5 caption: e.g. RCT 92.9, HYPERPARTISAN 94.8).

terms.definition: domain-adaptive pretraining: continued pretraining of RoBERTa on a large corpus of unlabeled domain-specific text
task-adaptive pretraining: pretraining on the unlabeled training set for a given task
TAPT using a larger human-curated pool of unlabeled task-distribution data
TAPT on task data plus k nearest domain sentences retrieved by VAMPIRE embeddings
